head: c120cfc
prompt:
this prompt is not for drafting a novel it is for updating the framework so don't feel held by agents.md. codex evaluated this framework and made some changes. Below I am pasting some feedback on it. See what you agree with and if you think the framework can be improved as a writing tool, make those changes. Feedback: 

<pasted_content id="0cbf">
The most important weaknesses:

1. Editing safeguards have real implementation holes. Disposable tests confirmed that scope checking accepts an unauthorized adjacent rewrite, TODO completion checks the working copy instead of the staged commit, and --files can commit unrelated already-staged work. These undermine the author-ownership promises.
2. Evaluation produces more confidence than the evidence supports. Three simulated personas are not three independent readers. Scores lack calibration, while sentence survival confounds quality with review coverage, attribution, and task difficulty.
3. Cold reads can receive spoilers. Mandatory preflight prints TODO directives and author commit subjects. Several reader-isolation instructions also conflict with general context-loading requirements.
4. The default cycle risks excessive administration and local refinement. Every-chapter critique, triage, canon updates, and periodic additional reports lack clear effort budgets or stopping rules.
5. Craft defaults can narrow the fiction. Repeated requirements for crises, value shifts, wounds, and particular arc structures may override the stated principle that these are optional lenses.
6. Story memory can become stale. Canon, summaries, timelines, character files, and plans lack source-revision tracking and explicit treatment of superseded facts.

My recommended technique is:

1. Establish a compact creative brief and strong voice exemplars.
2. Draft a meaningful narrative sequence, maintaining essential continuity.
3. Let the author read first and identify the most consequential uncertainty.
4. Choose the evaluation that answers that uncertainty.
5. Revise toward one specific reader effect.
6. Verify that effect, update affected memory, and stop when the objective is met.
7. Use independent human readers at meaningful milestones; resolve structure before polishing sentences.

For example, replace “improve this chapter” with “readers should suspect the brother while understanding why the protagonist trusts him.” That supplies a useful evaluation target without prescribing the prose.

Priority order: repair safeguards and add regression tests; enforce reader isolation; simplify routine passes; track memory freshness; then calibrate evaluations against human responses. Measure author review time, useful findings, continuity defects, and blind reading preference—not merely word production or rising AI scores.
</pasted_content id="0cbf">
